name: GridDistortion-TS-TW

frames.best_why: A wide patch of the mountain photo is pushed out of place in clear square steps beside the cursor.

tagline: Glides a photo into square ripples wherever the cursor passes.
summary: A photograph sits full-bleed, and moving the pointer drags nearby patches of it aside in a blocky grid. The displaced tiles ease back to their places once the cursor moves on.
appearance: One landscape photo fills the frame edge to edge, rounded at the corners, against a black surround. Over it sits a coarse invisible mesh, so warped areas show as offset rectangular tiles rather than smooth curves.
behaviour: Pointer movement shoves a cluster of square patches of the image sideways, strongest right under the cursor. When the pointer stops or leaves, the offsets decay and the picture settles back into place.
demo_content: Snowy mountain range above a sea of clouds at sunset, shot from a ridge.
search_phrases: photo that ripples under the cursor
hero photo that bends when touched
use_when: A single strong photo needs a playful hover effect, as in a hero or a case study banner.
avoid_when: You want a smooth liquid warp: the mesh is coarse and the result reads as square tiles.
customise: The image comes in as a required URL prop; mesh density, pointer radius, warp strength and how fast it settles are props too. The shader offset is fixed.
weight_why: A THREE renderer draws a displaced plane every frame for a live WebGL scene.

a11y.note: The effect is mouse-only and the photo has no alt text, so keyboard and screen-reader users get nothing.

issues: The warp breaks into hard square tiles, so it reads as a glitch grid rather than a smooth bend.
polish_why: The effect answers the cursor well, but the coarse blocks give away the low-res mesh.
